models.purpose: Bound the worst connectivity bottleneck of the floor-plan graph and name the corridors a Fiedler cut severs
models.summary: Rooms are vertices and doors, halls and stairs are edges of nearly equal travel time. The normalized Laplacian uses 1 on the diagonal, -1/sqrt(d_u d_v) on edges and 0 elsewhere. Conductivity Phi_G is the worst boundary-to-volume ratio of a set smaller than half the vertices. Chung's Cheeger inequality replaces that minimum by lambda_2/2 <= Phi_G <= 2 sqrt(lambda_2). With lambda_2 = 0.009287497 the paper reports 0.004643748 <= Phi_G <= 0.192743320, also written as 0.1115026 plus or minus 0.1056103. The Fiedler vector is roughly bimodal and a sign cut severs four corridors, one of them the Richelieu entrance, isolating that wing from every exit.

models.purpose: Place candidate hidden exits where they minimize mean shortest-path distance to an exit
models.summary: Hidden exits are absent from public plans. Algorithm 1 tries candidate rooms, flood-fills the shortest distance from every room to the nearest real or candidate exit, and keeps the candidate with the smallest mean of those distances. The chosen rooms are handed to the agent simulation.

models.purpose: Simulate one person at a time with a density-dependent exponential transfer time and hard blocking at capacity
models.summary: k events spread uniformly in time have Erlang gaps. Each person is moved separately, so k = 1 and the gap is exponential with rate mu. Crowd interaction makes the mean wait grow with density: mu = t_0 exp(c rho(u)), where t_0 is the empty-room mean time and c a penalty. A move into a full room is refused and redrawn. Time advances to the soonest scheduled edge. Responders obey the same rule with a smaller penalty c_s. Arrivals of 2532.83 people per hour and a 3 hour visit give a stock of 7598.49; a 72735 m^2 footprint and a safety code give a cap of 21748. Damage that leaves a dead end reverses the sign edge once the dead-end density passes a critical value.

models.purpose: Replace the stochastic transfers by a deterministic density ODE with a blocking term and a non-negativity term
models.summary: Crowd density is treated as a thick fluid in a porous layout. Scalar flow out of u is (1/t_0) exp(-c rho_u) times a non-negativity factor n(rho_u) times a blocking factor b(rho_v). In vector form the paper writes d(rho)/dt = [A B(rho) + E] Hadamard V^{-1} N(rho) minus [A^T V^{-1} N(rho)] Hadamard B(rho). Blocking is b_i = (1+2 rho_i)(1-rho_i)^2 and the source factor is n_i = (1/t_0) exp(-c rho_i) (3-2 rho_i) rho_i^2. Euler steps the system at one-second intervals. A room is bottlenecked at rho = 1, empty at 0, and at equilibrium when 0.1 < rho < 0.9. The authors report the model was too hard to tune for a deep analysis.
